mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate over the past three months (measured by the 3-month change in FEDFUNDS) predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >60% of instances with a 3-month decline in FEDFUNDS (FEDFUNDS[t] - FEDFUNDS[t-3 months] < 0), or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate exceeding 5.5% signals a weakening labor market that reduces consumer confidence and spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >60% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 5.5%, or the Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) over the past month signals a contraction in consumer and business demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline in the prior month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in >60% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS decline in the prior month, or the Rank IC for the joint signal over any 3-year rolling window is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%), a decline in industrial production over the past month signals a weakening real economy, which reduces corporate earnings growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines in the prior month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of instances where INDPRO declines in a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%), or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in the CPI (CPIAUCSL) signals persistent inflation, which may prompt the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of periods with a year-over-year increase in CPIAUCSL (CPIAUCSL[t] > CPIAUCSL[t-12 months]), or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in non-farm payrolls below 50,000 (PAYEMS monthly change < 50.0) signals a weak labor market, which reduces consumer spending and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >60% of instances where PAYEMS monthly change < 50.0, or the Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in quarterly GDP (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) over the most recent quarter signals a contraction in the real economy, which reduces corporate earnings growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline in the prior quarter
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in >60% of instances where both GDPC1 and HOUST decline in the prior quarter, or the Rank IC for the joint signal over any 3-year rolling window is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (UNRATE < 4.5%), a decline in industrial production over the past month signals an overheating economy that may prompt the Federal Reserve to tighten policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines in the prior month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of instances where INDPRO declines in a late-cycle expansion (UNRATE < 4.5%), or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is < 0.03.
